### 2026-10-07: ![images 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/hj9IuZu2HToxwkIcTWuCd0qtbAwUD0cg/44bd814a3b1cf9e3220e64996720947acda7082e53103cd6f38ebea13c204f1d.jpg)

**1h**

![images 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hj9IuZu2HToxwkIcTWuCd0qtbAwUD0cg/44bd814a3b1cf9e3220e64996720947acda7082e53103cd6f38ebea13c204f1d.jpg)

I began working on the script for the idea reel. Due to the fact that I cant use videos, Ive turned it into a basic mind map for this project

Basically  my project is  a music player that has an rfid reader that when It connects to a card it gets the id and plays the audio file from a repo.
I got this idea from one of my sister’s toys called a “yoto” it basically did what I just said and with the upcoming season of half-life, I thought, why not build something like a DIY yoto.

here is a simple Bill of materials:

Rfid scanner to scan rfid

Esp32 or other microcontroller

Small speaker to play the audio

3w-5w digital amplifier board

USB sound card

To rotary encoders to control volume and rwd/fst

A pcb to wire it all together

Although I haven't done that much hardware, I have a basic idea and have participated in hack club stardance, so I'm excited to work in this new club.

I began working on the schem for the DIY yoto project Im making.
So far, I have placed the required symbols, however Ive realized how long this was gonna take. for now, I'm using a

ESP32-S3-Wroom

Max98357A

Mfrc522 RFID module reader

U3 TP4056-42-ESOP8

2 rotary encoder switches

J1 Micro SD Card

I also had to design the symbol for the RFID reader Mod

Ok So this Is a general "improvement journal". Basically, I got my Week 1 project revised, and since I was editing along the way and journalling on the other projects, I kinda need to make a final journal here to write what I did

1.
I finished the Original PCB: This was in week 2.
I the reason why this took so long was cuz I didn't know how to do via jumping, so I was stuck trying to wire it all on one side. week 2 I learned how to, so I wired it all up

2.Finished the errors: this was end of week 2 I think. Basically, when I first wired it, I got like 100 DLC errors, but one time when I showed it to my dad, who knows Pcb fabrication and hardware, told me I can't have errors or warnings in the DLC, so I figured how to fix them all.

3. Netclasses: This was the Worst one of all, I think during week 3, when I realized that some wires for 5V power need thicker lines. I had originally thought that I did the auto net classes correctly, but I didn't, so I had to fix that.

4. SMD to THT: this happened week 5 I think, where I wanted to check on my week1 to make sure it was all good, but I realized that it was 90% SMD, and that costs way too much for me, so I had to switch to THT alternatives.

5.redoing BOM and README: This is the latest and final change. I got the project reviewed and it said that I should upgrade the BOM and README, and to make this journal in the first place!
